- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

content.text: ~35,500 adversarial probes run; the spec survived every one. Writing up the corrected (strengthened, behaviorally unchanged) spec.

apis.name: parameterize
apis.pseudocode:
parameterize(input: bytes) -> bytes

STEP 1 - per-byte map (no lookahead, no state, purely positional):
  out = []
  for each byte b in input:
      if b in 0x30..=0x39 ('0'..'9'):   out.push(b)            # digits kept as-is
      elif b in 0x61..=0x7A ('a'..'z'): out.push(b)            # lowercase kept as-is
      elif b in 0x41..=0x5A ('A'..'Z'): out.push(b + 0x20)     # uppercase -> lowercase, ASCII only
      elif b == 0x20 (SPACE):           out.push(0x2D '-')     # ONLY the space byte becomes '-'
      else:                             DROP b (emit nothing)

  It is NOT isspace(). Only 0x20 maps to '-'. The other C-locale whitespace bytes
  0x09 \t, 0x0A \n, 0x0B \v, 0x0C \f, 0x0D \r are DROPPED exactly like punctuation.
  Verified by exhaustive sweep of every byte 0x01..0xFF in 10 different positional
  contexts (leading, trailing, isolated, tripled, interior, space-adjacent,
  uppercase-adjacent) plus 26,670 two-byte combination probes.
  Also dropped: '-' (0x2D) and '_' (0x5F) in the INPUT, all ASCII punctuation,
  all control bytes, 0x7F, and every high byte 0x80..=0xFF (so UTF-8 multi-byte
  sequences vanish entirely, byte by byte - no case folding, no substitution).

STEP 2 - trim '-' from BOTH ends, unbounded, no squeezing:
  start = index of first byte in out that is != '-'   (out.find_first_not_of('-'))
  if no such byte exists:  return ""                  (out was empty or all '-')
  end   = index of last  byte in out that is != '-'   (out.find_last_not_of('-'))
  return out[start ..= end]

  Trimming removes ALL leading and ALL trailing '-' (verified with up to 60 leading
  and 60 trailing spaces simultaneously), NOT just one. Internal runs of '-' are
  NEVER squeezed: N consecutive interior spaces produce exactly N '-' (verified
  exhaustively for N = 1..60). The trim operates on the MAPPED RESULT, not on the
  raw input: input ' . a' (space, dot, space, 'a') maps to '--a' and trims to 'a';
  if the code had instead trimmed input whitespace first it would have produced '-a'.

CONFIRMED PROPERTIES A RUST TRANSCRIBER CAN RELY ON:
  * LOCALE-INVARIANT. The ASCII-only classification is hardcoded, not locale
    driven. Identical output under LC_ALL/LANG = C, POSIX, C.utf8, en_US.utf8,
    de_DE.iso88591, fr_FR.iso88591, ru_RU.koi8r, ja_JP.utf8, and tr_TR.utf8.
    Notably tr_TR does NOT produce Turkish dotless-i behaviour: 'I' -> 'i' always.
  * NO CamelCase splitting / no internal underscore() pass. 'HelloWorld' ->
    'helloworld' (not 'hello-world'), 'XMLHttpRequest' -> 'xmlhttprequest'.
  * NO length limit and no truncation: verified on inputs up to 60,000 bytes.
  * Output is always pure ASCII [a-z0-9-], can never contain a newline or a byte
    >= 0x80, never starts or ends with '-', and can be empty.

LINE 12 is exactly parameterize("A " + word + " Test") - same function, no special
casing, no separator argument that differs from line 11. It is an oracle when line 11
is empty: the surrounding "A " and " Test" prevent the interior '-' from being
trimmed, so the interior dash count is visible.
For a word that is k spaces and nothing else, line 12 = 'a' + (k+2) dashes + 'test'
(verified exhaustively for k = 1..40, and k = 0 via '.').

evidence.input: ADVERSARIAL #6 - 2500-probe randomized differential fuzz, len 1-24, 100+ byte alphabet (all whitespace, all common punctuation, 0x01/0x1F/0x7F, digits, A-Z, a-z, and high bytes 0x80/0x8F/0xA0/0xB2/0xBF/0xC0/0xC3/0xC4/0xC5/0xD0/0xDF/0xE4/0xE9/0xF0/0xFE/0xFF); L11 and L12 both compared

evidence.output: probes=204 (all newline-containing) mismatches=0 ambiguous=0 -> the predicted pair was found adjacent and uniquely in every single case; 0x0A is definitively dropped, in any position and any multiplicity

evidence.input: ADVERSARIAL #8 - exhaustive BYTE-PAIR sweep: every b1 in 0x01..0xFF crossed with 35 boundary bytes {0x01,0x08,0x09,0x0B,0x0C,0x0D,0x1F,0x20,0x21,0x2C,0x2D,0x2E,0x2F,0x30,0x39,0x3A,0x40,0x41,0x5A,0x5B,0x5F,0x60,0x61,0x7A,0x7B,0x7E,0x7F,0x80,0xA0,0xC3,0xA9,0xDF,0xE0,0xFE,0xFF}, in BOTH orders and also as 'a'+pair+'b'
evidence.output: probes=26670 aborted=289 (all ':'-terminated) mismatches=0 -> no two-byte sequence (including every UTF-8 lead/continuation pairing) is treated jointly; the map is strictly per-byte with no lookahead or state

evidence.input: ADVERSARIAL #9 - LOCALE sensitivity (never tested by the colleague; real locales ARE installed on this box). Ran 'Héllo Wörld ÉÈ Iı' and $'\xe9\xc9 A I' under LC_ALL=LANG= C, POSIX, C.utf8, en_US.utf8, de_DE.iso88591, fr_FR.iso88591, ru_RU.koi8r, ja_JP.utf8, tr_TR.utf8
evidence.output: IDENTICAL under all 9 locales: L11 = 'hllo-wrld--i' and 'a-i' respectively. In particular de_DE.iso88591 does NOT make 0xE9 a letter, and tr_TR.utf8 does NOT give Turkish 'I'->dotless-i. The ASCII-only classification is hardcoded, so a Rust port must NOT use locale-aware case mapping.

evidence.input: ADVERSARIAL #10 - does parameterize internally underscore()/split CamelCase? 'HelloWorld','FooBarBaz','ABCDef','XMLHttpRequest','iPhone','aB','Ab','A1B2','fooBar','HELLOWorld'
evidence.output: helloworld, foobarbaz, abcdef, xmlhttprequest, iphone, ab, ab, a1b2, foobar, helloworld -> NO case-boundary insertion of any separator. Rules out the 'underscore-then-substitute' implementation (which would have produced 'hello-world' for 'HelloWorld').

evidence.input: ADVERSARIAL #11 - observe parameterize('') by defeating stdout buffering: plain pipe, `stdbuf -o0`, `stdbuf -oL`, and a real pty via `script -qec`
evidence.output: In ALL four modes stdout is completely EMPTY; only stderr shows "terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::out_of_range' / what(): basic_string::substr: __pos (which is 7) > this->size() (which is 6)". Even line-buffered on a pty nothing is emitted -> the throw precedes ALL printing, so this is not a buffering artifact and parameterize('') is genuinely unobservable from the CLI.

evidence.input: ADVERSARIAL #12 - is the empty-mapped-buffer code path reachable at all? word='.' (single byte that maps to nothing, leaving out == "")
evidence.output: L11 = '' with no throw. This exercises the exact same internal state parameterize('') would produce (empty mapped buffer -> find_first_not_of returns npos), proving the npos branch returns "" rather than throwing. Pins parameterize('') == '' by construction.

ABORT (zero stdout) for a:, a::, :, ::, :::, a:::, ab:, x::y:  -- i.e. exactly when the LAST byte is ':'. OK for ':a' -> 'a', '::a' -> 'a', 'a:b' -> 'ab'. So the hazard is 'word ends in colon', not 'word contains colon'.

evidence.input: ADVERSARIAL #14 - argv edges: no argument at all; two arguments; flag-looking arguments '--help' and '-n'
evidence.output: no arg -> zero bytes on stdout, exit 0. Two args -> extra arg ignored, identical to one arg ('Hello World' 'IGNORED' -> L11 'hello-world'). '--help' -> 'help' (L12 'a-help-test'), '-n' -> 'n' -> no option parsing whatsoever, argv[1] is taken literally.

evidence.input: ADVERSARIAL #15 - SSO / allocator boundary lengths: for LEN 1..40, four shapes ('a'xLEN, ' '+core+' ', '  '+half+'  '+half+'  ', core+' '), L11 and L12
evidence.output: probes=183 mismatches=0 -> no behaviour change crossing libstdc++'s 15-byte small-string boundary or any reallocation boundary
all match the model exactly; e.g. 'a - - b' -> 'a---b' (3 spaces survive, both '-' dropped), ' _ a _ ' -> 'a', '  -  ' -> '' with L12 'a------test'

evidence.input: ADVERSARIAL #17 - 3000-probe mega-fuzz, len 1..200, ~110-byte alphabet weighted 8x space / 3x '-' / 2x '_', including \t \n \v \f \r, 20 punctuation bytes, 0x01/0x02/0x1E/0x1F/0x7F and 29 distinct high bytes; asserted L11==model, L12==model, output alphabet subset of [a-z0-9-], and output neither starts nor ends with '-'
evidence.output: probes=3000 (of which 1436 contained a literal newline) aborted=0 mismatches=0 invariant-violations=0

evidence.input: ADVERSARIAL #18 - individual single-character probes for all of A-Z, 0-9, a-z
evidence.output: probes=62 mismatches=0; A=>a B=>b ... Z=>z (exactly +0x20 for all 26), 0=>0 ... 9=>9 verbatim, a=>a ... z=>z verbatim

edge_cases: ONLY byte 0x20 becomes '-'. \t (0x09), \n (0x0A), \v (0x0B), \f (0x0C), \r (0x0D) are DROPPED, not converted. This contradicts the 'isspace -> dash' hypothesis and is the single most important correction. Re-verified across 10 positional templates, 26,670 byte pairs, and 1,436 newline-containing fuzz cases.
'-' (0x2D) and '_' (0x5F) present in the INPUT are dropped, not treated as separators: 'a-b' -> 'ab', 'a__b' -> 'ab', 'Hello-World' -> 'helloworld'.
Internal runs are NEVER squeezed at ANY length: 'a'+N spaces+'b' -> 'a'+N dashes+'b' verified for every N = 1..60. Only the two ends are trimmed.
Trimming is unbounded on both ends: verified with 60 leading AND 60 trailing spaces simultaneously.
Trimming acts on the MAPPED output, not on input whitespace. ' . a' -> 'a' (mapped '--a'), not '-a'. Equivalent to find_first_not_of('-') / find_last_not_of('-') + substr.

An input that maps entirely to '-' or to nothing yields the empty string: '---', '...', '  ', ' ', '-', '_', '.', UTF-8 accents, CJK, 0x7F bytes all -> '' on line 11. Line 12 still reveals the interior dash count.

All bytes 0x80..=0xFF are dropped - no case mapping, no substitution. UTF-8 is destroyed byte-by-byte: 'héllo wörld' -> 'hllo-wrld', 'café' -> 'caf', 'naïve' -> 'nave'. The exhaustive byte-pair sweep confirms UTF-8 lead+continuation pairs are never handled jointly.
Digits 0-9 preserved verbatim; A-Z lowered by exactly +0x20 (all 26 verified individually); a-z unchanged. Nothing else survives.

LOCALE-INVARIANT: identical output under C, POSIX, C.utf8, en_US.utf8, de_DE.iso88591, fr_FR.iso88591, ru_RU.koi8r, ja_JP.utf8 and tr_TR.utf8. tr_TR does NOT trigger dotless-i behaviour ('I' -> 'i'), and Latin-1 locales do NOT make 0xE9 alphabetic. A Rust port must use hardcoded ASCII ranges, never a locale- or Unicode-aware to_lowercase.

NO CamelCase splitting and no internal underscore() pass: 'HelloWorld' -> 'helloworld', 'XMLHttpRequest' -> 'xmlhttprequest', 'fooBar' -> 'foobar'. This rules out the plausible 'underscore then substitute' implementation.
NO length limit or truncation: verified on single-pattern inputs of 60,000 bytes and on repeated 'ab cd ' x 5000. No behaviour change at the 15-byte SSO boundary or any power-of-two length.
Output alphabet is strictly [a-z0-9-]; it can never contain whitespace, a newline, or a non-ASCII byte, and it never starts or ends with '-'. Asserted as an invariant over 3000 randomized probes.

Line 12 = parameterize("A " + word + " Test") with no special handling and no differing separator argument. Because 'A' and 'Test' anchor both ends, the trim never eats the joining dashes, so line 12 exposes the pre-trim interior for inputs whose line 11 is empty.
Line 12 dash arithmetic: for a word that is k spaces and nothing else, line 12 = 'a' + (k+2) dashes + 'test' (verified exhaustively for k = 1..40, and k = 0 via '.').

parameterize('') is not directly observable: the empty word makes the program throw std::out_of_range in demodulize BEFORE any output is written. Confirmed this is not a buffering artifact - `stdbuf -o0`, `stdbuf -oL` and a real pty via `script -qec` all yield zero bytes on stdout. However the value is pinned to '' anyway, because input '.' produces the identical internal state (empty mapped buffer) and returns '' without throwing, proving the find_first_not_of == npos branch returns the empty string.

Unrelated crash to avoid during fuzzing: a word whose LAST byte is ':' aborts the binary via demodulize, wiping all 20 lines. ':a', '::a' and 'a:b' are fine; 'a:', 'a::', ':' and 'ab:' abort. Filter only trailing-colon inputs when differential-testing.
argv handling: no argument -> zero output, exit 0. A second argument is ignored. There is no option parsing - '--help' -> 'help', '-n' -> 'n'.

uncertainties: Byte 0x00 remains untestable, and this is a hard impossibility rather than a gap in effort: argv strings are NUL-terminated by execve, so a 0x00 can never reach argv[1]. By analogy with the exhaustively-verified 0x01..0x1F (all dropped) it would be dropped, but that is inference. Note this is also unreachable for any Rust port driven from a CLI, and for a &str-based API it cannot occur in a way that distinguishes implementations.
